## Nulla Vitae

_Vestibulum id ligula porta felis euismod semper. Sed posuere consectetur est
at lobortis. Let us walk the evaluation metrics._

_Mean Squared Error averages the squared gaps between predicted and observed
values, which makes it sensitive to outliers:_

$$
\text{MSE} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2
$$

_Root Mean Squared Error returns those units to the scale of the target:_

$$
\text{RMSE} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2}
$$

_Mean Absolute Error averages the magnitude of the error while ignoring its
direction:_

$$
\text{MAE} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \left| y_i - \hat{y}_i \right|
$$

_And the coefficient of determination reports the share of variance in the
target explained by the features, bounded at one:_

$$
R^2 = 1 - \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2}{\sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \bar{y})^2}
$$

_Cras mattis consectetur purus sit amet fermentum. Results below are printed
from the fitted object rather than typed into the prose, so the narrative can
never drift out of step with the numbers:_

```{python}
print(f"Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)  : {metrics['RMSE']}")
print(f"Mean Absolute Error (MAE)       : {metrics['MAE']}")
print(f"R-squared                       : {metrics['R2']}")
```
